name: models
description: Discover which LLM providers and models are ready on this venue for your identity. Load before selecting or overriding an agent's llmOperation/model.

content.inline:
## Models
Call `v/ops/langchain/models` `{provider?}` -> `{providers: [{op, provider, keySecret?, ready, defaultModel, models, recommendations?, url?, note?}]}`.

Reading the answer:
- ready is caller-relative. For hosted providers it means your secret store or the venue environment supplies keySecret; the value is never shown and readiness does not validate the credential remotely. For Ollama it means the configured server is reachable, and models is the live installed set.
- defaultModel is the balanced built-in choice when no model is supplied. recommendations maps workload labels such as economical, quality, coding, or longRunning to a supported model id.
- Hosted model lists are release-time selections, replaceable by venue configuration. Any model id accepted by the provider may still work.

Choosing:
- Prefer a provider with ready=true, then choose for the workload rather than always taking the largest model. Add a later config layer such as `{llmOperation: <op>, model: <id>}`.
- Usually omit apiKey: each provider operation resolves its configured default secret. Set `apiKey: "s/<name>"` only to override that binding.
- If a hosted provider is not ready, load secrets and store the named key. If Ollama is not ready, its note identifies the relevant venue setting.
- For tool-using Ollama agents, choose a model whose advertised capabilities include tools. Do not infer support from the family name.
- Anthropic is the built-in venue fallback and Sonnet 5 its balanced default. Haiku is economical; Opus/Fable are for more demanding work. Anthropic honours maxTokens (a venue default applies). temperature/topP pass through where supported.

Templates are provider-neutral: an explicit later provider layer wins. Without one, creation materialises the venue's configured default, which falls back to Anthropic. Check readiness before delegating when provider availability matters.
